When we stressed tested our data center we were looking at about $1000/test of about an hour or so to simulate a real load.

Well, really though for the most part, a "stress test" is a lot of cases is basically a DDOS. They even told us that when we signed up and started building out our scripts. They flat out told us that we have to be careful with their services because if you throw 100,000 users at the servers it seriously will act like a DDOS. They also recommended we tell our ISPs.

Yes, I understand that a stress test is basically a DDOS, but my point is that a botnet could be built by somebody and used without it costing a costing a large sum of money. They could maliciously slave machines whose users are not even aware they are part of a botnet, negating basically any cost. It was my understand, and again correct me if I am wrong, that when a website is DDOSd, not stress tested, the attackers are not using a stress testing service, but are using slaved machines of users who are unaware they are part of a botnet.
